belief: Natural disasters are God punishing the people they strike.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that natural disasters are God punishing the people they strike, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Public figures who blame disasters on the sins of certain groups. Teaching that every tragedy is a direct judgment. Trying to make sense of devastating events. Fear that a disaster in your life means God is angry with you. Confusing the general brokenness of creation with specific punishment.
teaches: God is sovereign over creation, and Scripture records some specific judgments. But Jesus directly rejected the idea that victims of disasters are worse sinners. When a tower fell and killed eighteen people, He said they were not more guilty than others. The whole creation is groaning under the effects of sin, and God sends sun and rain on the righteous and the unrighteous alike. Disasters remind all of us of our need for God, and they call us to compassion, not judgment, toward those who suffer.
self_statements: Those people must have deserved it.
God sent that disaster to punish them.
If a disaster hits me, God is angry with me.
I can tell who God is punishing by what happens to them.
Victims should examine what they did wrong.
errors: Deciding the cause of a disaster without God’s revelation.
Seeing a disaster in your own life as proof of God’s anger.
Overlooking His direct words in Luke 13.
questions: What did Jesus say about the eighteen who died when the tower fell?
Were they worse sinners than others?
What does Matthew 5:45 say about sun and rain?
Why is all of creation groaning, according to Romans 8:22?
What does God want, according to 2 Peter 3:9?
Does this belief make me more compassionate or more judgmental?
How can I help people affected by disasters?
truth: Natural disasters are not proof that God is punishing the people they strike. Jesus said the victims of tragedy were not worse sinners than others. All creation groans under sin’s effects, and disasters touch the righteous and unrighteous alike. They remind all of us of our need for God and call me to compassion, prayer, and help.
hw_questions: What did Jesus say about the tower’s victims?
What does God want for everyone?
Does this belief make me compassionate or judgmental?
hw_truths: Disaster victims are not worse sinners than others.
All creation groans under sin’s effects.
God sends sun and rain on everyone.
Disasters remind all of us of our need for God.
I am called to compassion, not judgment.
God will one day make all things new.
log: Each day, pray for people affected by a disaster or hardship, and write one way I can help.
name_example: The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with Sarah, not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.
actions: and write what Jesus said about tragedy and repentance.

prayer: Father, my heart breaks when disasters strike. Help me reject the lie that natural disasters are You punishing the people they strike. Give me compassion instead of judgment, move me to help those who suffer, and fill me with hope that You will make all things new. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
